POST /api/proof-documents/network-share -> resolveNetworkPartnerProofView looks up any proofDocument by attacker-supplied proofId gated only by attacker-settable unsigned cookie partnerShareScope==='network'. claimedCustomerId is parsed but never used in the query (line 506), so any authenticated user reads proof metadata (fileName/category/jobId) of any tenant's proof, bypassing the customerVisible/ownership checks enforced by getScopedProofDocument and the verified variant (lines 536-542).

This authentication, registration or account-recovery surface answers differently (error wording) depending on whether the submitted account identifier resolves to an existing account, so an attacker can enumerate valid accounts by probing identifiers alone.

POST /api/jobs/:id/charge calls recordJobCharge with attacker-controlled job id but performs no object-level check (no canManageJob, unlike sibling credit-memo route at line 1378). Any authenticated user (customer/field_worker) can overwrite amountCents on any job; recordJobCharge at line 378-385 updates by id with no scope predicate.

An AES-CBC decryption failure (invalid padding) is distinguishable from other failures through an externally observable response (tagged-result), without a prior authentication/integrity check — a CBC padding oracle.

GET /api/service-notes/:id (and /api/service-notes/lookup/:reference at line 1659) call getServiceNoteById with attacker-controlled note id. getServiceNoteById (line 460-475) reads any job_messages row by id with no job-ownership or visibility check, so a customer can read internal-visible messages of other customers' jobs that job detail view (lines 322-337) would hide.

A dispatcher can mutate serviceDate/status of a route belonging to another region.
